claims.title: The Kunda culture
claims.summary: Mesolithic hunter-fishers of the Kunda culture, named for the Estonian town of Kunda, settled the eastern Baltic forest zone after the Ice Age, among the earliest inhabitants of the region.

sources.label: Ancient Estonia and the Kunda culture

claims.title: Foundation of the Brothers of the Sword
claims.summary: Bishop Albert of Riga established the Livonian Brothers of the Sword, the military order that, with the Teutonic Knights and the Danes, drove the Northern Crusades into Estonia.

claims.summary: Danish crusaders defeated the northern Estonians and built a fortress on Toompea hill, giving rise to Tallinn (Reval); northern Estonia became a Danish duchy within Terra Mariana.

claims.summary: Sweden ceded Estonia and Livonia to Russia, which organised them into governorates and confirmed the privileges of the Baltic German nobility, beginning two centuries of Russian imperial rule.
